Multiscale Procrustes-Based 3‑D Shape Control

Shape control deforms a non-rigid object into a desired shape with robots. In this paper, we control the 3D shape of texture-less objects that undergo large deformations, without a model of the object and without an initial exploration of its behavior. Functional maps match the points of the perceived mesh to those of the target mesh, and a multi-scale Procrustes analysis defines the 6 DoF action of each gripper.

The scales are geodesic distances to the grippers. For each scale, the Procrustes analysis of the points within that distance gives the rigid motion that would align them with their targets. The controller estimates which of these motions reduces the shape error, validates the estimates against the measured response of the object (local-rigidity behavior), and moves the grippers along \SE geodesics at a locally optimal scale \rs(t).

These pages first introduce the idea on flat pieces in 2D, and then compute the analysis and the closed loop in 3D in the browser, on objects simulated with ARAP as in the simulations of the paper, and evaluate the terms of the stability proof along the way.

Ignacio Cuiral-Zueco and Gonzalo López-NicolásUniversidad de Zaragoza (I3A)IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics, 29(3), 2024

01

The idea in 2D

The method on flat pieces moved in their plane, step by step: the geodesic ball of radius r, the rigid-part model at r against the simulated object, the estimation of r from observed motions, and the closed loop in \mathrm{SE}(2).

02

Multi-scale analysis

Secs. II-A to II-D. Geodesic balls about the grippers, the Procrustes transform of every ball, the estimate of the local-rigidity model for an action scale and an influence scale, the error increments, their validation, and the effectiveness q(t,r).

Shape control

Secs. II-E and IV-A. The closed loop on five objects simulated with ARAP: the isolines of the selected scale, the gripper poses that the Procrustes transforms prescribe, the estimate of the LRB model against the simulated response, and the map q(t,r) with \rs(t).

Stability

Video

the control scheme, the simulations, and the experiments of the paper

The video presents the control scheme, from the 3D mesh of the object to the multi-scale analysis and the definition of the actions at the locally optimal scale. It then shows six simulations with ARAP (anti-symmetric bending, a beam with an appendix, grippers placed near the center of the object, a pure twist, a pure stretch, and a bend of 180°), each with the shape error, the deformation of the object, q(t,r) with \rs(t), and the actions.

The four experiments follow, with the segmented camera images, the meshes from the top, side, and front, the error, q(k,r) with r^*(k), and the actions: bending and twisting of an elongated piece, an unfolding in which the object buckles, a pure twist, and the 3D bending of a triangle (3 min 51 s). Code

the MATLAB implementation of the paper, and the source of these demos

The repository of the paper contains a MATLAB implementation of the method (main.m and multiscaleprocrustescontrol.m) with a precomputed surface map, which simulates the object with the ARAP implementation of gptoolbox on a tetrahedral mesh generated by iso2mesh.

% MATLAB R2022b, with gptoolbox, iso2mesh, and the utilities of dependencies.zip
main                       % one simulation with ARAP, plots, and demo-video.avi

The demos are static files (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with KaTeX and three.js included) in the folder docs of the same repository, next to the web version of the paper (docs/paper). The simulation modules (docs/js/sim) also run in Node.js, where tests/test_sim.mjs checks them.

python run.py                  # http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/build_web.py      # after editing the sources in docs (needs Node.js)
node tests/test_sim.mjs        # checks of the simulation modules
